messages.author: ea85553bd7ffeaf9
messages.subject: file.choose() problem on glimmer.rstudio.com
parts:
Hi:

I built a simple shiny application to rename image files in a local folder to correct the naming scheme for a project I'm working on (e.g., NY-F-00012345.jpg to NY-F-00012345_L00.jpg).

The app was tested locally on a mac and worked fine; however, after loading the app to http://glimmer.rstudio.com/stbates/img_rename_app/, the file.choose() call I put behind an actionButton from shiny-incubator no longer works.  

I've tested the actionButtons and they are active, but the call for file.choose() that is part of a function to extract the folder path from the file selected won't work - the choose file dialog box doesn't open when I press the actionButton to call the function.

The code for the application can be found here:

https://github.com/stbates/img_rename_app

Thanks...

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: file.choose() problem on glimmer.rstudio.com
parts:
Hi Scott,

The file.choose() function launches an Open dialog box right out of the R process. In this case, the R process is running on our server and is not interactive (interactive() == FALSE), so R knows that file.choose() can never succeed.

Where are the files you want to rename? Are they on the server, or on your Mac? If on the server, one (ugly) workaround would be to have a textbox where you can paste in the full path of the folder.

messages.subject: Re: file.choose() problem on glimmer.rstudio.com
parts:
Hi Joe:

Thanks for your speedy reply - this makes sense.

I would like someone accessing the app to be able to select a folder on their own computer and then rename all the image files in that folder (e.g., without having to have R installed on their local machine).  

The idea with file.choose() was to have the user select a file in the folder on their computer with the image files to be renamed - then extracting the path to the folder for renaming all the image files there.

It sounds like the non-interactive status of the R process running on the server won't allow for this.

BTW - shiny has a lot of potential - thanks for your development.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: file.choose() problem on glimmer.rstudio.com
parts:
Oh, then what you're trying to do isn't possible--you can't have an ordinary web application (which is what Shiny apps are) rename files on the visitor's machine. It would be a massive security problem if you could.

I'm sure you could use a Java applet to do it, or something else that is not a web application.
